annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT), Qatar
key_provisions_or_claims: Eight voluntary principles: do no harm, robustness/security/safety, anti-bias, environment, privacy, transparency, human-centered approach, human accountability
Pre-deployment risk assessments, continuous updating, referencing NCSA secure AI guidelines
AI should not autonomously make decisions of significant consequence; humans can appeal or override
External audits for AI informing significant decisions
Autonomous vehicles need rigorous pilots and testing on diverse conditions such as deserts
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology issues voluntary, non-binding guidelines setting eight principles for ethical AI development and deployment, aligned with Qatar National Vision 2030, UNESCO and OECD norms. It mentions autonomous vehicle safety briefly; otherwise it addresses general AI risk, bias, privacy, transparency and human accountability.
annotation.title_clean: Artificial Intelligence in Qatar – Principles and Guidelines for Ethical Development and Deployment
annotation.title_en: Artificial Intelligence in Qatar – Principles and Guidelines for Ethical Development and Deployment
